subject: Physics
title: Electromagnetic Waves
summary: Maxwell added the displacement current ε₀ dΦ_E/dt to Ampère's law: a changing electric field makes a magnetic field, just as a changing magnetic field makes an electric field. Together they let fields travel as waves.
Electromagnetic waves are transverse: E, B and the direction of travel are mutually perpendicular. In vacuum they travel at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, and E₀ = cB₀.
They carry energy and momentum; intensity I = ½cε₀E₀². Electric and magnetic fields share the energy equally.
The spectrum, from long to short wavelength: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays — each with typical sources and uses.

formulas.name: Displacement current
formulas.note: Inside a charging capacitor I_d equals the conduction current in the wires.

formulas.name: Ampère–Maxwell law
formulas.when: Why a changing E field produces B.

formulas.name: Speed of light
formulas.formula: c = 1/√(μ₀ ε₀) = 3 × 10⁸ m/s;  in a medium v = 1/√(μ ε) = c/n
formulas.when: EM wave speed in vacuum and media.

formulas.name: Field amplitudes
formulas.formula: E₀ = c B₀  (E = cB at every instant)
formulas.when: Finding B from E or vice versa.
formulas.note: B₀ is tiny (E₀/3 × 10⁸) — that doesn't mean the magnetic energy is small.

formulas.name: Wave equations
formulas.formula: E = E₀ sin(kx − ωt) ĵ,  B = B₀ sin(kx − ωt) k̂;  c = ω/k
formulas.when: Writing or reading an EM wave.

formulas.name: Direction of propagation
formulas.when: Finding which way the wave moves.

formulas.name: Energy density
formulas.formula: u = ½ε₀E² + B²/2μ₀ (equal shares);  average u = ½ε₀E₀²

formulas.name: Intensity
formulas.formula: I = u_avg × c = ½ c ε₀ E₀²
formulas.when: Power per unit area carried by the wave.

formulas.name: Momentum and radiation pressure
formulas.note: A perfect reflector feels twice the pressure of a perfect absorber.

formulas.name: Spectrum order
formulas.formula: radio > microwave > infrared > visible (700–400 nm) > ultraviolet > X-rays > γ-rays  (wavelength decreasing)

topics.title: Why displacement current was needed
topics.explain: Ampère's law gave different answers for surfaces through a wire and through the gap of a charging capacitor. Maxwell's displacement current fixed this and predicted EM waves; Hertz produced them in 1887.

topics.title: Characteristics of EM waves
topics.explain: Transverse, need no medium, travel at c in vacuum, are produced by accelerated charges, obey superposition, can be reflected, refracted, diffracted and polarised, and carry energy and momentum. Frequency does not change from medium to medium.

topics.title: Radio waves and microwaves
topics.explain: Radio (> 0.1 m): produced by oscillating charges in antennas — AM, FM, TV, mobile communication. Microwaves (1 mm–0.1 m): klystrons and magnetrons — radar, satellite links, microwave ovens (they make water molecules vibrate).

topics.title: Infrared and visible
topics.explain: Infrared (700 nm–1 mm): emitted by hot bodies — heat lamps, remote controls, night vision, physiotherapy; keeps Earth warm through the greenhouse effect. Visible (400–700 nm): the only band our eyes detect.

topics.title: Ultraviolet
topics.explain: Produced by very hot bodies like the Sun and by special lamps. Kills germs (water purifiers), used in LASIK eye surgery; mostly absorbed by the ozone layer. Excess UV is harmful to skin and eyes; ordinary glass absorbs much of it.

topics.title: X-rays and gamma rays
topics.explain: X-rays (0.01–10 nm): made by fast electrons hitting a metal target — medical imaging, cancer therapy, crystal structure. Gamma rays (< 0.01 nm): from nuclear reactions — destroying cancer cells, sterilising equipment.
